Täitja kohustub oma kulul esindama tellijat lepingu alusel täidetavate ülesannete või toimingutega seotud kõigis vaidlustes (sh kohtuvaidlustes) kolmandate isikutega ning kandma kõik sellega kaasnevad menetluskulud. 7.7 Tellija võib lepingu üles öelda, kui Täitja rikub oluliselt õigusaktidest või lepingust tulenevaid kohustusi. Programme Aim The purpose of this training programme is to design, develop and deliver a training programme that build people’s understanding of self-harm and the role it plays in the life of a person who self-harms. The programme will build the knowledge and confidence of the learner to have a conversation if they are concerned that someone may be self-harming. The training programme should provide people who access it with a sense of hope and reassurance that people can build healthier coping mechanisms. Programme Objectives The training programme is intended to: Increase understanding of what self-harm is. Increase understanding of the relationship between self-harm and suicide. Build skills and confidence to engage with a person and speak openly about self-harm. Challenge the stigma surrounding self-harm Increase awareness of available supports and services Stage 1: An introduction to the subject of self-harm – communicating the ‘why’ functions of self-harm through lived experience experts. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Consultant brochures may also be included in the Expression of Interest (EOI).

 

5. Evaluation Criteria

Expressions of Interest will be evaluated using a 100-point scoring system based on the following criteria and weights:

Criterion 1: General experience of the firm (30/100)

This criterion assesses the firm’s overall experience and track record, including years of relevant experience and the number and type of websites successfully delivered.  Criterion 2: Experience in Similar Assignments within the last 10 years (25/100)

This criterion assesses the firm's experience in successfully delivering assignments of similar nature, scope and complexity to the required se

s currently reflected in the REOI.

Criterion 4: Experience with Government Institutions, Donor-Funded Projects and NGOs within the last 10 years (20/100)

This criterion assesses the firm's experience in providing similar services to government institutions, donor-funded projects, international organizations, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs). It evaluates the firm's familiarity with the working environment, requirements and standards typically associated with such organizations.

The firm shall provide relevant portfolios and supporting documents to substantiate the information provided under the above evaluation criteria. Such documents may include, where applicable, website links, project references, completion certificates, client references, or other evidence demonstrating the Applicant’s experience and qualifications.

The Expression of Interest should not exceed 50 pages.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.13, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (February 2025), which set forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

STATEMENT OF WORK C. 1. OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory

The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory of NLS DA2 devices. NLS requires quantities suffi
